cases.evidence_note: F1 pass, T-113. Expected values written from the archived source before the evaluator was run: the facts and values of stage19.example.jack_kay (p970 p. 19, a $2,500 American opportunity credit) with the dependent's ATIN only applied for by the due date. p970 p. 11, "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as is- sued on or before the due date of the return." The American opportunity credit is unchanged.

p970 p. 19, Figuring the Credit, Example: joint return, dependent child in the junior (third) year, MAGI $70,000, qualified education expenses $4,300, "Jack and Kay can claim a $2,500 American opportunity credit in 2025. This is 100% of the first $2,000 of qualified education expenses, plus 25% of the next $2,000." Class A covers lines 27, 30, 1 and 7 ($4,000 and $2,500). The 40%/60% split (line 8 $1,000, line 9 and line 19 $1,500, Form 1040 line 29 $1,000) follows from the form, not the example; line 19 is $1,500 because the scaffolded tax exceeds it. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): the $70,000 MAGI is taxpayer W-2 wages; the child is 20, a full-time student, a qualifying child for the credit for other dependents only; all $4,300 is paid to the institution; "meet all of the requirements" is read as a 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No (a junior has not completed 4 years), line 26 No. Shown state (from the forms, not the example; T-232): Form 8863 Part III for the child reaches lines 24, 25 and 26 (line 23 No, "No—Go to line 24"; line 24 Yes, "Yes—Go to line 25"; line 25 No, "No—Go to line 26"). No student has line 31, so line 10 is zero: "If zero, skip lines 11 through 17". EIC Worksheet A line 3 is not reached: i1040gi p. 42, Step 5 question 3, earned income of $70,000 is not "less than ... $57,554 if married filing jointly" for one qualifying child (nor $26,214 for none), "No. STOP You can't take the credit." Credit Limit Worksheet B is not completed: i1040s8812, "Complete Credit Limit Worksheet B only if you meet all of the following", which include claiming a listed credit (no Form 5695 Part I here) and "Line 4 of Schedule 8812 is more than zero" (the 20-year-old is not under 17, so line 4 is 0).

p970 p. 28, Example: joint return, MAGI $75,000; Toni already has a bachelor's degree and paid $5,000 of qualified education expenses for the fall 2025 semester; "Bruce and Toni can claim a $1,000 (20% x $5,000) lifetime learning credit on their 2025 joint tax return." Class A covers lines 31, 10, 11, 12 and 18. Line 19 $1,000 follows because the tax exceeds it. The bachelor's degree is read as line 25 Yes (first 4 years completed before 2025), so the American opportunity credit is unavailable and lines 1 and 8 are zero. Synthetic scaffolding: Toni is the spouse entry; the $75,000 MAGI is taxpayer W-2 wages; the $5,000 is paid to the institution; Form 1098-T and EIN available; lines 23, 26 No, line 24 Yes.

p970 p. 20, Phaseout, Example: joint return, MAGI $165,000, $5,000 of qualified education expenses, tentative credit $2,500, ($180,000 - $165,000) / $20,000, "The result is the amount of your phased out (reduced) American opportunity credit ($1,875)." Class A covers lines 30, 1, 3, 4 and 7. Line 8 $750 and line 9 and line 19 $1,125 follow from the form (joint, so line 7 is refundable at 40%; the tax exceeds $1,125). The example does not say who the student is: the taxpayer is the student (adult, so the line 7 age test does not arise; joint in any case). Synthetic scaffolding: MAGI is taxpayer W-2 wages; the $5,000 is paid to the institution; Form 1098-T and EIN available; lines 23, 25, 26 No, line 24 Yes. The ratio 0.750 is exact, so the rounding ambiguity is not exercised. Shown state (from the form, not the example; T-232): Form 8863 Part III for the taxpayer reaches lines 24, 25 and 26 (line 23 No, "No—Go to line 24"; line 24 Yes, "Yes—Go to line 25"; line 25 No, "No—Go to line 26").

p970 p. 29, Phaseout, Example: joint return, MAGI $161,000, $6,600 of qualified education expenses, "a $1,320 (20% x $6,600) tentative credit", ($180,000 - $161,000) / $20,000, "The result is the amount of your phased-out (reduced) lifetime learning credit ($1,254)." Class A covers lines 31, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 18. Line 19 $1,254 follows because the tax exceeds it. The example does not name the student or say why the American opportunity credit is not used: the taxpayer is the student and has completed the first 4 years (line 25 Yes), so only the lifetime learning credit applies. Synthetic scaffolding: MAGI is taxpayer W-2 wages; the $6,600 is paid to the institution; Form 1098-T and EIN available. The ratio 0.950 is exact. Shown state (from the form; T-232): Form 8863 line 4 is $19,000 ($180,000 less $161,000; "If zero or less, stop" does not apply) and line 10 is $6,600, so lines 11 through 17 are completed ("If zero, skip lines 11 through 17" does not apply).

i8863 p. 5, Coordination with Pell grants, Example 1: $5,000 of qualified education expenses, a $5,000 Pell grant applied to them as a tax-free scholarship; "you will have $0 ($5,000 - $5,000) of adjusted qualified education expenses available to figure your credit. Your credit will be $0." Class A covers line 27 (worksheet line 2a $5,000) and the zero credit on lines 30, 1, 7, 8 and 19. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): the parent files single with $60,000 of W-2 wages; the child is 18, a full-time student and the parent's qualifying child (credit for other dependents only; no EIC at this income); the $5,000 is paid to the institution; "meet all other requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No (first semester), line 26 No. The parent is not the student; the parent is an adult born before 2002, answered for the Form 8863 line 7 test, which a non-joint filer is asked about themselves. The child's own return (the $4,000 included in the child's income) is not modeled.

i8863 p. 5, Example 2: only $1,000 of the Pell grant applied to qualified education expenses; "you will have $4,000 ($5,000 - $1,000) of adjusted qualified education expenses available to figure your credit. Your refundable American opportunity credit will be $1,000. Your nonrefundable credit may be as much as $1,500, but depends on your tax liability." Class A covers line 27 $4,000, line 8 and Form 1040 line 29 $1,000, and line 9 $1,500 (the "as much as" amount). Line 19 $1,500 is the scaffolded case where the tax exceeds $1,500. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): the parent files single with $60,000 of W-2 wages; the child is 18, a full-time student and the parent's qualifying child (credit for other dependents only; no EIC at this income); the $5,000 is paid to the institution; "meet all other requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No (first semester), line 26 No. The parent is not the student; the parent is an adult born before 2002, answered for the Form 8863 line 7 test, which a non-joint filer is asked about themselves. The child's own return (the $4,000 included in the child's income) is not modeled.

i8863 p. 5, Example 2, last sentence: "If you're not otherwise required to file a tax return, you should file to get a refund of your $1,000 refundable credit, but your tax liability and nonrefundable credit will be $0." Class A covers line 8, Form 1040 line 29 and the $1,000 refund (lines 33, 34), line 19 $0 and line 22 $0. Line 9 $1,500 follows from the form. The "not otherwise required to file" parent is scaffolded with no income at all (no W-2), single, claiming the 18-year-old student child; the other scaffolding is as in pell.ex2. Shown state (from the form; T-232): the 18-year-old is not under 17, so Schedule 8812 line 16b is $0 ("Number of qualifying children under age 17 ... x $1,700 ... If zero, stop here; you cannot claim the additional child tax credit"), and Part II-A stops there.

p970 p. 15, Example 1, no scholarship: AGI and MAGI $39,250, standard deduction $15,750, "taxable income of $23,500 and an income tax liability before credits of $2,585", "qualified education expenses of $4,000, which results in a credit of $2,500 and a tax liability after credits of $85 ($2,585 - $2,500)." Class A covers lines 11b, 15, 16, 27 and 7; lines 8 $1,000, 19 $1,500, 22 and 24 $1,085 and 29 $1,000 follow from the form and are the form reading of the $85 (line 24 $1,085 less line 29 $1,000). No EIC at this AGI. Bill is 28, unmarried (single), first-year full-time student in a degree program; "Bill and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply. Synthetic scaffolding: the AGI the example states without a source is W-2 wages with no withholding; the $5,600 of qualified education expenses is paid to the institution (room and board are excluded and not entered). The publication's "tax liability after credits" nets the $1,000 refundable credit (Form 1040 line 29) against the tax; on the form the nonrefundable $1,500 reduces line 22 and the $1,000 is a payment.

p970 pp. 15-16, Example 2, scholarship excluded from income: a $5,600 scholarship usable for any expense, excluded from income; "Bill's adjusted qualified education expenses would be zero, and there would be no education credit. Therefore, Bill's tax liability after credits would be $2,585." Class A covers line 27 $0 (worksheet line 2a $5,600), lines 7 and 19 $0, and lines 16, 22 and 24 $2,585. The scholarship does not exceed the period's expenses (line 2a equals line 1). Bill is 28, unmarried (single), first-year full-time student in a degree program; "Bill and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply. The publication's "tax liability after credits" nets the $1,000 refundable credit (Form 1040 line 29) against the tax; on the form the nonrefundable $1,500 reduces line 22 and the $1,000 is a payment.

p970 p. 16, Example 3, scholarship partially included in income: $4,000 of the $5,600 scholarship included in income (Schedule 1 line 8r) and deemed applied to room and board; the remaining $1,600 reduces expenses (worksheet line 2a); "the adjusted qualified education expenses would be $4,000. Bill's AGI and MAGI would increase to $43,250, the taxable income would increase to $27,500, and the tax liability before credits would increase to $3,065", credit $2,500, "the tax liability after credits would be $565 ($3,065 - $2,500)." Class A covers lines 8r, 11b, 15, 16, 27 and 7; lines 8 $1,000, 19 $1,500, 22 and 24 $1,565 and 29 $1,000 are the form reading of the $565. Example 4 (the scholarship paid directly to the college) has the same inputs and results and is not a separate case. Bill is 28, unmarried (single), first-year full-time student in a degree program; "Bill and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply. Synthetic scaffolding: the AGI the example states without a source is W-2 wages with no withholding; the $5,600 of qualified education expenses is paid to the institution (room and board are excluded and not entered). The publication's "tax liability after credits" nets the $1,000 refundable credit (Form 1040 line 29) against the tax; on the form the nonrefundable $1,500 reduces line 22 and the $1,000 is a payment.

p970 p. 16, Example 5, scholarship excluded: "The AGI and MAGI would be $24,125. The tax liability before any credits would be $51. The qualified education expenses would be reduced to $500. Jane would be able to receive a $251 American opportunity credit ($200 refundable and $51 nonrefundable), a $1,700 additional child tax credit, and a $4,204 EIC. In total, Jane would be able to receive a tax refund of $6,104." Class A covers lines 11b, 16, 27, 8, 19, 29, 28, 27a and 33/34. Line 7 $500 and line 22 $0 follow (the $51 tax is fully offset, so the nonrefundable child tax credit is zero and the whole $1,700 is refundable). Worksheet line 2a $5,500, Schedule 1 line 8r $0. Jane is 28, unmarried, files head of household with her 10-year-old qualifying child (EIC and child tax credit), first-year full-time certificate student; wages $24,125 on a W-2 with no withholding and no other income or adjustments, except the scholarship she includes in income, entered on Schedule 1 line 8r. "Jane and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply. Synthetic scaffolding: head of household (the example says unmarried with a dependent child; household.home_cost Yes); the $6,000 is paid to the institution; the scholarship allocated to tuition does not exceed the period's expenses. The publication's "American opportunity credit" total is the allowed amount: Form 8863 line 8 (refundable) plus line 19 (nonrefundable, limited by the tax).

cases.evidence_note: Stage 19 mutation scenario: blind return E1 claiming the American opportunity credit after a denial that needs Form 8862 (or within a ban), refused (D1).

f8863.line7.form: Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, or a ban on the American opportunity credit
f8863.line7.remedy: An American opportunity credit after a denial or reduction (other than for a math or clerical error) needs Form 8862, and a credit within a 2- or 10-year ban is not allowed; this tool does not prepare either.

cite.locator: p. 1, Form 8862 may be required, "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit."

The filer's dependency answer is person[taxpayer].sav_claimed (true), the question Form 8863 and the student loan worksheet read for this test.

You’re claimed as a dependent on another person’s tax return, such as your parent’s return." The return of stage19.mut.claimed_filer_llc with no student loan interest and no student loan worksheet answer: the filer answers person[taxpayer].sav_claimed true, so f8863.claimed_count is 1 and f8863.eligible is false; lines 10, 11 and 19 are $0 and Form 1040 line 29 is $0. Shown-state regression (T-232): stage19.blind.e3 with wages of $95,000 (W-2 boxes 1, 3 and 5) instead of $62,000. Predicted from the archived f8863 before evaluating: line 3 (modified AGI, here AGI) is $95,000, more than line 2 ($90,000 for head of household), so line 4 is zero and Part I stops there (f8863 line 4, "Subtract line 3 from line 2. If zero or less, stop; you can't take any education credit").

Mutation fixture (T-159: the half-support operand of person.edu_kid), predicted from the archived f8863 and i8863 before evaluating: stage19.blind.e1 (single, the filer an American opportunity credit student, line 7 $1,296.41) with the filer aged 18 at the end of 2025 (born after January 1, 2007), not a full-time student, with earned income less than one-half of support and a living parent. Line 7 condition (b), "You were age 18 at the end of 2025 and your earned income was less than one-half of your support", with at least one parent alive and no joint return, is met (i8863 line 7): the refundable credit is not allowed, line 8 is $0.

Mutation fixture (the age 19 to 23 alternative of person.edu_kid_student_age), predicted from the archived f8863 and i8863 before evaluating: stage19.blind.e1 (single, the filer an American opportunity credit student, line 7 $1,296.41) with the filer aged 19 to 23 at the end of 2025 (born after January 1, 2002, before January 2, 2007), not a full-time student, with earned income less than one-half of support and a living parent. i8863 p. 6: "You don't qualify for a refundable American opportunity credit if 1 (a, b, or c), 2, and 3 below apply to you"; 1(c) needs a full-time student and 1(a) and 1(b) age 18 or under, so condition 1 is not met and the credit stays refundable, and line 8 is 40% of line 7, $518.56, as in stage19.blind.e1.

Mutation fixture (the line 7 not-needed alternative of person.edu_kid), predicted from the archived f8863 and i8863 before evaluating: stage19.blind.e1's student filing a joint return (the spouse has no income), aged 19 to 23 at the end of 2025, with the line 7 questions (full-time student, earned income less than one-half of support, a living parent) withheld. i8863 p. 6: the refundable credit is barred only if conditions 1, 2 and 3 all apply, and 3 is "You're not filing a joint return for 2025"; on a joint return the questions of condition 1 and 2 are not needed: no filer is counted for line 7 and the credit is not barred from being refundable.

Mutation fixture (T-159: the line 4 operand of f8863.ban_refused and the line 7 operand of f8863.kid_needed), predicted from the archived f8863 and i8863 before evaluating: stage19.blind.e1 (single, an American opportunity credit student, line 1 $2,387.50) with wages of $95,000 (W-2 boxes 1, 3 and 5) and the filer answering that an earlier American opportunity credit was denied (Form 8862) or is within a ban.
